Then test 2.25 and 3.25 in later rounds to map the demand curve. If 2.25 gives higher total profit than 2.75, explore below it (about 1.90 to 2.10). 1.insights: With no data, a reasonable prior assumes willingness to pay is spread across 1.00 to 4.51. Under a uniform-demand assumption, expected profit is (p - 1) * (4.51 - p) / 4.51, which peaks at p = (4.51 + 1.00) / 2 = 2.755. So 2.75 is a sensible starting point. This is a hypothesis only and must be checked against real sales data.
